subject: microbiology
title: Poliovirus, Salk and Sabin Vaccines, VDPV and AFP Surveillance

steps.tx: **Poliovirus** is a non-enveloped enterovirus with three serotypes transmitted mainly faecal-orally. Most infections are asymptomatic or mildly febrile. A minority invade the central nervous system and destroy anterior horn motor neurons, causing asymmetric flaccid paralysis with intact sensation. Wild poliovirus types 2 and 3 have been certified eradicated, while endemic type 1 transmission persists in limited reservoirs.
steps.say: Polio paralysis is rare per infection but devastating and permanently motor selective.

left.title: Infection spectrum
points: Minor illness with fever and malaise
Paralytic disease in under one percent

steps.tx: The **Salk vaccine** is inactivated poliovirus vaccine, IPV, given by injection. It produces strong serum IgG that prevents viraemic spread to the nervous system but induces weaker intestinal mucosal immunity than oral vaccine. It cannot replicate, revert or cause vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis. IPV is therefore preferred in immunodeficiency and in polio-free settings concerned about vaccine-derived circulation.
steps.say: IPV protects the nervous system without any risk of vaccine virus replication.

right.title: IPV limitations
points: Can allow some gut infection and shedding
Multiple doses or fractional schedules used

steps.tx: The **Sabin oral polio vaccine** contains live attenuated virus that replicates in the gut, inducing local IgA and serum antibody and sometimes spreading secondarily to contacts. That intestinal barrier made OPV ideal for interrupting outbreaks. Its rare costs are vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis and emergence of vaccine-derived polioviruses where population immunity is too low to stop continued circulation and reversion.
steps.say: OPV blocks the gut powerfully, but underimmunised circulation lets vaccine virus evolve back.

right.title: OPV risks
points: Type 2 component removed from routine trivalent OPV

steps.tx: **Vaccine-derived poliovirus** is Sabin virus that has regained neurovirulence and transmissibility through prolonged replication, usually in underimmunised communities or rarely within an immunodeficient person. Novel oral polio vaccine type 2 was genetically stabilised to reduce reversion risk during outbreak response. Detection of VDPV in stool or sewage is an eradication emergency requiring rapid high-coverage vaccination.
steps.say: VDPV is an immunity-gap signal, not an argument against vaccination itself.

left.title: Categories
points: Type 2 has dominated since wild type 2 eradication

right.title: Response
points: Use vaccine matched to VDPV type
Strengthen routine coverage in the source area

steps.tx: **Acute flaccid paralysis surveillance** requires reporting and investigating flaccid weakness in children and any suspected polio at any age. Two stool specimens collected at least twenty-four hours apart within fourteen days of onset maximise poliovirus isolation because shedding declines with time. Surveillance quality indicators include notification speed, stool adequacy and non-polio AFP rate, proving the system would detect imported wild virus.
steps.say: Two timely stools are the laboratory backbone of AFP surveillance.

steps.tx: AFP has many causes besides polio, including **Guillain Barre syndrome**, transverse myelitis, traumatic neuritis, acute flaccid myelitis from other enteroviruses and hypokalaemic paralysis. Symmetry, reflexes, sensation, progression and cerebrospinal fluid help separate them, but surveillance requires stool testing even when another diagnosis seems likely. This avoids missing poliovirus hidden inside a familiar syndrome.
steps.say: AFP surveillance tests first and classifies later so polio cannot hide behind Guillain Barre.

left.title: Polio clues
points: Reflex loss localised to affected limbs

right.title: Other AFP clues
points: GBS is usually symmetric and ascending
Transverse myelitis has a sensory level
Traumatic neuritis follows injection or injury
Periodic paralysis is episodic and potassium linked
